newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes extend premium to futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes extend premium to futures.

text.p: U.S. domestic cash crude prices extended their premium to futures Thursday, benefitting from the second straight month of sizable foreign crude deliveries against paper contracts.
NYMEX said earlier Thursday that nearly all of the 2.372 million barrels of physical crude delivered against paper matches was foreign in content.
Trade sources said Nigerian Bonny Light made up most of the 2.349 million foreign barrels delivered, forcing Bonny receivers to ante up a 60 cents premium for each barrel.
Traders said the foreign deliveries were not necessarily bullish or bearish for grade differentials, but did extend the positive run for cash West Texas Intermediate/Cushing over NYMEX futures.
"WTI (cash) holds a 25-30 cents premium to the futures. These deliveries are bullish for EFPs (Exchange for Physicals)," said a crude trader.
July EFPs were valued at a 15 cents premium Thursday, gaining around seven cents from Wednesday, indicating more foreign deliveries were expected for July.
EFPs are an insurance policy for refiners or trade houses wanting to avoid deliveries other than WTI. The agreements allow a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for physical position.
Traders said they expected June's foreign deliveries to find their way into storage ahead of possible re-delivery in July.
"Another 2.3 million (foreign crude deliveries) is possible, and Cusiana is coming as well," said a trader.
The Bonny Light premium will be reduced from 60 cents to 40 cents from July 1.
"This will only stop when the Brent-WTI spread collapses or refineries find a way to make money from running the Bonny," said a trading source.
Around the market Thursday afternoon, June domestic grade barrels found only nominal interest. Friday is pipeline scheduling day for June supply, and most business was completed earlier this week.
July Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was sold at stronger prices from 15-10 cents under benchmark levels. Firmer wet Brent deals propped the LLS market, sources said.
Outright July WTI/Cushing was five cents higher at $21.85-95 a barrel, and held a 20 cents edge on roll trades with June WTI/Cushing.
